question: which compiled rules can run, per cell context, and why the rest cannot

structure.network: a compiled rule's source is an element, never a gene: the census counts rules whose source is a gene entity, and if that count is 0 a run integrates one independent one-gene system per regulated gene, so nothing a run reports depends on any other gene
structure.level: the bridge fits each resolved gene so that its intact steady state is T / delta_m in every cell it resolves (split_measured_rate: intact transcription = T), so the predicted level of a gene does not depend on any compiled rule and is the same in every cell
structure.on_off: every resolved gene has basal_rate > 0, because the split reports one that does not as rate_split_infeasible; a run therefore predicts 'on' for every resolved gene in every cell, with its element present or absent, and cannot predict 'off' anywhere
structure.in_its_own_cell: with the element clamped present and absent in the rule's own cell, a run returns the observation it was fitted to (bridge.RATE_ACCEPTANCE; S5: 'direction and fold for all (they are the input)')

reading: a gene-cell pair is resolved when the bridge fits its one mechanism; the borrowed tier resolves in relative units only and is never a measured count. Pairs are counted per program, so a gene whose rules sit in two programs (the X/Y pseudoautosomal genes) counts once in each; the registered run pools mechanisms over programs before it admits a pair
money: none: no request is sent and no key is read

sources.version: the files on this machine, pinned by sha256 in inputs
the committed file, pinned by sha256 in inputs

result_manifest.assembly: GRCh38, the assembly the compiled programs were written on; no interval is read
result_manifest.coordinates: n/a: counts of rules, mechanisms and gene-cell pairs per cell context

tiers.measured: the gene's own measured T, carried to its human symbol through a 1:1 homology class
tiers.borrowed: the genome median of the measured T, for a gene with no measurement. It fixes no absolute number: such a pair is simulable in RELATIVE units only, is counted separately and is never added to the measured count

parameters.rate_species: Mus musculus, NIH 3T3 fibroblasts; every human simulation using them borrows a mouse constant
parameters.panel: the 54 compiled contexts named for GTEx v8 tissues (runrules.PANEL)
parameters.no_measured_rna_read: the census opens no expression value of any kind

result_manifest.partitions: n/a: every compiled rule is counted, held-out or not

entry_script.why: argv[0] is a file inside this repository that git tracks and reports unmodified: the commit holds the code that wrote the bytes, so a rebuild can run it. The only clean form
entry_script.forms_are_decided_in_advance: genomeos.manifest.ENTRY_FORMS: one clean form (a tracked, unmodified file inside this repository), every other form refuses, and a form that cannot be classified is 'unknown' and refuses too. Read from sys.argv[0] at write time, never declared

code_cleanliness.counting_path_is_computed: the transitive import closure of this script, computed from the files' import statements at write time (genomeos.manifest.counting_path), never by importing: it follows every import that resolves to a file in this repository rather than only the package, counts the __init__.py of each package above a module, resolves bare imports against the directories the source literally puts on sys.path as well as the repository root, and matches every path component against what its directory lists, so a class name such as genomeos.genome.Genome cannot enter it as a file; not a hand-written list
code_cleanliness.note: several lanes work in this one checkout. A file under foreign_uncommitted_code belongs to another lane; this lane did not write it and did not commit it. The counting path is the computed closure above, so a foreign file outside it cannot have entered a number here, and foreign_uncommitted_code_on_the_counting_path names any that could

revision_stamps.sampled: code_cleanliness.git_sha is read while the writer computes; code.git_sha is read when the result is written. Both are HEAD of the same checkout at two moments
revision_stamps.reading: no revision race: both stamps record 37ece3a

traced_inputs.note: Every file this writer opened for reading under data/ was recorded by an audit hook on the "open" event, canonicalised through data/'s links so one file has one spelling, and compared against the inputs the manifest declares; a member of a declared group counts as declared and hashed on its own, a file under a declared directory counts as declared by prefix. The hook is per interpreter, so a file read by a subprocess is not in this record, nor is one reached through a path that canonicalises to neither this checkout's data/ nor one of its link targets.
